answer: Admission to basalt mapping, nebula imaging and grove surveying queues requires a fresh proof of computational work for each agent key. The verifier hashes the queue name, key, daily random seed and a nonce, accepting only hashes with 24 leading zero bits; it records each admission once. A proof for one queue or key is invalid for another, so ten aliases require ten separate searches averaging 2^24 trials each. This prices fake admissions in computation, though specialized hardware can make them cheaper.
